clue.text: Lose Scottish-island after onset of mist

indicators.note: after places the island's name behind the letter taken from mist
the onset of a word is its beginning, so only the opening letter of mist is used

parts.note: Islay is an island of the Inner Hebrides, off western Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone loses their way on a Scottish island when the mist rolls in.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislay something is to put it somewhere and then lose track of it.

clue.text: What a joiner gets in limbs and joint

parts.note: members is an old word for the limbs of the body
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A carpenter suffers aches in arms, legs and joints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiner' suggests a carpenter, but here it is someone who joins a club, and the pieces are body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who joins a club or society is granted belonging, the status of being one of its members.

clue.text: Stay downstairs late, and suddenly become alert

explanation.surface: A household member stays up downstairs and then is jolted awake.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay up late rather than go to bed, and to straighten and take notice, are both senses of the phrase.

clue.text: Bring about pain that is very internalised

indicators.note: internalised means taken inside, so the abbreviations go within the word for pain

parts.note: an ache is a dull pain
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is
V is the abbreviation for very, as in v. good

explanation.surface: Suffering that is kept bottled up produces a result.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve something is to accomplish it, to bring it about by effort.

clue.text: Firm initially falls behind with fashionable leading product

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of Firm is wanted

parts.note: to lag is to fall behind
hip is slang for fashionable

explanation.surface: A company slips behind its rivals despite a stylish top product.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagship is the best or most important product in a range, named after a fleet's lead vessel.

clue.text: Oppressed youngster's extremes of emotion

parts.note: a lad is a youngster, a boy

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A teenager goes through emotional highs and lows.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means weighed down or burdened, as one oppressed by worries is.

clue.text: Ship's engineer wanting good rubber changing around the heads?

indicators.note: the opening two letters of the word for rubber swap places, its head letters changed round

parts.note: an eraser is a rubber, for removing pencil marks

explanation.surface: A ship's mechanic lacks a good rubber for replacing the drive heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' is a link meaning 'needing to be'; 'changing around the heads' swaps only the first two letters of the rubber, and 'heads' is not a drive part but word beginnings.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship a greaser is an engine-room rating who lubricates the machinery, a junior engineer.

clue.text: Anticyclone comes down the upper part of Scotland

parts.note: an anticyclone is an area of high pressure, a high in weather forecasts
to land is to come down to the ground

explanation.surface: A weather report: high pressure settles over northern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Highlands are the mountainous northern region of Scotland, its upper part both in height and on the map.

clue.text: One who explored the Niger by power boat

parts.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
an ark is a vessel, as in Noah's

explanation.surface: An explorer travelled up the Niger in a motorboat.
explanation.walkthrough: Mungo Park was a Scottish explorer who travelled the Niger river in West Africa around 1800.
explanation.definitionFit: Mungo Park, the Scottish surgeon, led expeditions tracing the course of the Niger.

clue.text: Argument against last of cream going in a portion of soup

parts.note: a con is an argument against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: going in means entering, so the letter is put inside the word for a portion

parts.note: some means a portion, an amount of something

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a dollop of cream being stirred into their soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of cream' gives M, which goes into SOME to make SOMME.
explanation.definitionFit: Consommé is a clear soup made from concentrated stock.

clue.text: Table protector's cold and hot bowl splinters

parts.note: a mat protects a table from hot dishes
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
in the game of bowls a wood is one of the balls bowled

explanation.surface: A table mat is spoilt when hot and cold bowls shatter on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link here. In the British lawn game of bowls the balls are called woods.
explanation.definitionFit: Matchwood is wood broken into tiny pieces, as in smashed to matchwood, so it means splinters.

clue.text: Keen to hear bore speaking?

indicators.note: speaking signals the word for bore is pronounced rather than written

parts.note: an auger is a tool for boring holes

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious to hear a tedious person talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a tedious person, but it is the tool that bores holes; 'to hear' joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager means keen, impatient for something.

clue.text: Explore senses changing with frequency to make clear personal feelings

indicators.note: changing means the letters of the two words rearrange into a new order

parts.note: F is the symbol for frequency in physics

explanation.surface: Someone explores their senses so as to articulate their emotions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges EXPLORE SENSES into EXPRESSONESEL, and F is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To express oneself is to put one's thoughts and personal feelings into words.

clue.text: Whirling imams aren't entirely conventional?

indicators.note: whirling means spinning round, so the letters of imams aren't are spun into a new order

explanation.surface: Whirling dervish imams are not wholly conventional, it is suggested.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe of aren't is ignored, leaving IMAMSARENT, ten letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The mainstream is the prevailing, conventional current of opinion or taste.

clue.text: Succeeded with fish spear

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies
a pike is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone manages to catch a fish with a spear.
explanation.definitionFit: A spike is a sharp point, and to spike is to pierce, so it matches spear as noun or verb.

clue.text: I omit clip when cycling unwise

indicators.note: cycling suggests the letters going round and round into a new order

explanation.surface: A cyclist skips using a trouser clip, which is foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Impolitic means unwise or tactless, not prudent in the circumstances.

clue.text: Met morn and day but never finished official minutes

indicators.note: never finished means each word lacks its ending, so the final letter of every one is removed

explanation.surface: A committee met morning and day but never got through its business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a link. Dropping the last letter of each of Met, morn, and, day leaves ME MOR AN DA.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoranda, plural of memorandum, are written records or notes, such as official minutes.

clue.text: When article's included in very enthusiastic Times title here?

indicators.note: included in means placed within, so the two short words go inside

parts.note: mad, as in mad about, means very enthusiastic
as can mean when, as in as I left
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper fan grows excited when a piece appears in The Times.
explanation.definitionFit: A masthead is the title of a newspaper printed at the top of its front page, where The Times' name appears.

clue.text: Perhaps a mite's nip damaged busy Lizzie

indicators.note: damaged means harmed, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A mite's bite may have harmed a houseplant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' is a link; the apostrophe in mite's is ignored. Busy Lizzie is the British name for a popular flowering bedding plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Busy Lizzie is the common name of Impatiens walleriana, a plant of this genus.

clue.text: Announced limit to fuel, causing confusion

indicators.note: announced means said out loud, so the words are taken as sounded

parts.note: a term is a limit or end, and oil is fuel, put together

explanation.surface: A declared cap on fuel supplies causes chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmoil is a state of great disturbance or confusion.

clue.text: Officer on board holding seaman during a roll

indicators.note: during places the seaman within the period of the roll, so inside it

parts.note: a bun is a bread roll
OS stands for ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A ship's officer clings to a sailor as the vessel rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' is a link; 'roll' suggests a ship's motion, but it is a bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A bosun, or boatswain, is the ship's officer in charge of equipment and crew on deck.

clue.text: British Standard aimed at has brought in grand sarcastic response

indicators.note: has brought in means taken inside, so the letter goes within the standard

parts.note: an ideal is a standard of perfection that is aimed at
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A British Standards body has brought in a large target, prompting scorn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British Standard' looks like one unit (the BS mark) but splits: British gives B, 'Standard aimed at' gives IDEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Big deal! is an ironic retort meaning that something is not impressive at all.

clue.text: One who was crowned and strangely glad thereafter

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: A newly crowned monarch was oddly happy afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred the Great was a ninth-century king of Wessex, so he was one who wore a crown.

clue.text: Senseless, in one way, to drink cold coffee

indicators.note: to drink means to take in, so the letter goes inside the word

parts.note: deaf is lacking one sense, hearing

explanation.surface: Someone, numb in one way, drinks a cold coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Decaf is short for decaffeinated coffee.

clue.text: Hard to deal effectively with rising age

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters read upward, so backwards

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
to cope is to deal effectively with something

explanation.surface: It gets hard to manage as one grows older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns the whole run HCOPE upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a long period of time, an age or era.

clue.text: Using disc, lefthander that's marking the pitch

indicators.note: using means making use of some of the letters in the words that follow, a run inside them

explanation.surface: A left-handed thrower uses a discus on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' suggests a sports field, but it is musical pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A clef is the sign at the start of a stave showing the pitch of the notes.

clue.text: Significant sum towards house

parts.note: a lot is a large amount, a significant sum
to means towards, as in walking to town

explanation.surface: A large sum is put down towards buying a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' looks like a dwelling, but it is the game also called housey-housey, a form of bingo.
explanation.definitionFit: House, or housey-housey, is an old British name for bingo, a game like lotto.

clue.text: Duenna providing tea for each single

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
per means for each, as in per person
one means single

explanation.surface: A chaperone serves tea to every unmarried person.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman who acts as a chaperone to a young lady in Spain or Portugal.

clue.text: Stand in front of lobby doors perhaps for renovation

parts.note: to face something is to stand in front of it
a lift, a British word for an elevator, has doors that open onto a lobby

explanation.surface: Someone stands before doors in a lobby that need refurbishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A facelift is a renovation that improves the appearance of a building, by extension from cosmetic surgery.

clue.text: With ecstasy behold that one God

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
lo is an old word meaning behold
him can mean that one, a man pointed out

explanation.surface: In rapture, a worshipper beholds the one God.
explanation.definitionFit: Elohim is a Hebrew name for God used in the Old Testament.
